clippings.speaker: Ron Perlman
clippings.quote: What I didn't realize was the campaign he mounted over the course of 6 years. He really could have made the film on 20 different occasions if he had used this actor or that actor or this actor. … It's the most generous gesture I have ever witnessed and certainly been the recipient of.
clippings.title: Hellboy: An Interview with Ron Perlman
clippings.context: Press interview for Hellboy, asked how it felt knowing del Toro would not make the film without him.

clippings.speaker: Ron Perlman
clippings.quote: First and foremost, from the moment we met, even before we started shooting "Cronos", there was this instant friendship. Regardless of whether we ever worked together or will work together in the future, this friendship will endure. So, working with your best pal on something that you both are such geeks over which is moviemaking and cinema in general is as good as it gets.
clippings.title: Hellboy: An Interview with Ron Perlman
clippings.context: Same Hellboy press interview, on their third collaboration and how they met.

clippings.speaker: Ron Perlman
clippings.quote: Everybody accused me of improvising my way through the first Hellboy, but everything I said was scripted by Guillermo and it just sounded like me. I don’t know how he did it, but I had this gift bestowed upon me and you never want to look a gift horse in the mouth.
clippings.title: I, Hellboy: An Interview with Ron Perlman
clippings.context: Interview by Ed Gross tied to the Hellboy II DVD release, on del Toro's writing of the character.

clippings.speaker: Guillermo del Toro
clippings.quote: Hellboy’s a guy you could hang out with and kick back a couple of six packs with, and then all of a sudden he has to go out and kick some monster ass. Ron has that nonchalant, very aloof attitude, but has a very powerful voice and presence, too.
clippings.title: I, Hellboy: An Interview with Ron Perlman
clippings.context: Del Toro explaining Perlman's casting, quoted in the introduction to a Perlman interview; original setting not stated.

clippings.speaker: Guillermo del Toro
clippings.quote: Ron and I were talking while we were making Cronos; I was at his house. We had watched Gunga Din and then Elmer Gantry. He said, “You know, there’s a movie called Nightmare Alley, with Tyrone Power, and I would love to remake it.” I went and got the book, by William Lindsay Gresham.
clippings.title: Guillermo del Toro talks about bringing Nightmare Alley To the Big Screen
clippings.context: Q&A with del Toro on Nightmare Alley, asked how Perlman was the progenitor of the adaptation some 30 years earlier.

clippings.speaker: Guillermo del Toro
clippings.title: Dreaming of Hell: A Reflection on Guillermo del Toro’s ‘Hellboy’ Journey Following His Beyond Fest Appearance
clippings.context: Said at a 2025 Beyond Fest appearance, recalling how he fought studios that pitched bigger names for the role.
